argument_summary: The certification decision should be evaluated on a narrower theory than the overbroad claim the audit flagged. The admissible record supports operational launch readiness: aggregate readiness passed by 2.1 points, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the rollout is limited to 7% with monitoring and rollback. The same record also shows a real unresolved limitation: the retirement plan servicing segment is below target on hardship withdrawal explanation, remains exposed in the initial cohort, and is not covered by approved risk acceptance. On that record, the defensible position is not that rollout controls cure the weakness. It is that certification can be treated only as caveated and only if the packet is understood to rely on required launch-time disclosure of the exposed limitation rather than claiming the disclosure predicate is already proven in evidence.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalating this record as flat noncompliance would overweight the governance gap and underweight the admissible evidence showing bounded initial exposure, reversibility, and live monitoring. The business cost of escalation is launch delay despite a record that supports a narrower, caveated certification posture. A caveated treatment preserves appropriate scrutiny without treating the readiness and control evidence as irrelevant.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not allow monitoring, rollback, or small rollout percentage to substitute for disclosure when the affected use case remains exposed. The admissible evidence supports that point. The narrower policy-consistent reading is that operational controls support the launch decision on risk-mitigation grounds, while the unresolved exposed limitation still requires disclosure unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. The audit concern is valid to the extent it rejects any claim that rollout controls alone are sufficient; it is overbroad if it treats the operational-readiness evidence as having no governance value at all.
concessions: The current admissible record does not prove that launch-time model-card disclosure has already been prepared, approved, or attached to the release packet.
The risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, unapproved, and does not address the exposed retirement plan servicing segment.
Any claim that monitoring and rollback alone make the launch compliant would conflict with the policy text.
